scams.name: Alanya 'Buy Drinks' Card-Skimming Bar Scam
scams.description: A friendly 'local' approaches you on Bar Street and invites you to a 'nice bar nearby.' You buy four drinks. The card terminal is brought to your table. The waiter taps the screen multiple times saying it 'didn't go through.' By the next morning you discover your card has been charged €800–€2,500 in additional 'transactions' to bars you never entered. The card was skimmed: while pretending to retry the payment, the staff captured your card data and made multiple high-value charges through the same terminal or sister venues. Community reports consistently document the social-engineering opening: a fluent-English 'local' who initiates conversation specifically to steer tourists toward a flagged venue. Travelers warn: 'Just came back after being in Alanya. Fantastic place with amazing people! But yeah, def many tourist traps' which include both bar-card scams and overcharge bars. The Turkey-wide rule: never let your credit card leave your sight in any bar. For older travelers, particularly solo male travelers, the protective playbook: (1) NEVER follow an unsolicited 'friendly local' to a bar you haven't chosen yourself; (2) at any bar, pay cash for drinks (small bills only — never ₺500 notes); (3) if you must pay by card, watch the terminal stay at your table and refuse 'didn't go through, let me try again' retries; (4) if asked to 'sign here' on a paper receipt, photograph the amount before signing; (5) check your bank app immediately after each transaction; (6) if you suspect skimming, freeze the card via your bank app within 60 seconds and call your bank's fraud line; (7) report the venue to Tourism Police 155 with venue name and address.
scams.avoidance: NEVER follow an unsolicited 'friendly local' to any bar in Alanya Pay cash for drinks at bars (small bills, never ₺500 notes) If using card, watch the terminal stay at your table; refuse 'didn't go through' retries Photograph the amount on any signed paper receipt BEFORE signing Freeze card via banking app within 60 seconds of suspected skimming
scams.location: Alanya bars on Bar Street (Damlataş Caddesi) and Cleopatra Beach promenade, side-street venues off the main strip, late-night returns from Karaalioğlu Park area

scams.name: Cleopatra Beach Taxi & Boat Excursion Overcharge
scams.description: Cleopatra Beach is Alanya's most famous beach — 2 km of fine sand named after the legend that Mark Antony gifted it to Cleopatra. The legitimate licensed taxi fare from Alanya center to Cleopatra Beach is approximately ₺140–₺200 (€3.50–€5) on the meter. One traveler wrote: 'They try to scam you, portIcall beach to Cleopatra should be less than ₺300 lira but at least ₺140 lira. They don't want to run the meter' and quote 'fixed prices' of ₺500–₺800 instead. For boat excursions, the legitimate Alanya 'pirate boat' day-tour with 5–6 swim stops costs ₺600–₺900 per person (€15–€22) including lunch through vetted operators. Below that tier, beach touts sell €10–€12 'special boat tours' that turn out to be 2-hour shorter trips with hidden ₺200 'mandatory tip' demands at end. Community reports document the broader excursion-reseller pattern with the recurring question of whether travelers are being scammed and, if so, by whom. Reports from 2024 confirm an escalation in beach-tout aggression. For older package-holiday travelers, the protective playbook: (1) for taxis, insist on the meter and confirm ₺140–₺200 range to Cleopatra Beach before boarding; (2) use BiTaksi app for app-regulated fares with digital receipts; (3) for boat tours, book through your hotel concierge or vetted operators (Alanya Pirate Boat with posted prices) at ₺600–₺900 per person; (4) decline beach-tout offers under €15 — the math forces shortcuts; (5) confirm in writing: lunch included, all drinks at posted prices, no 'mandatory tip,' specific number of swim stops; (6) for the short walk back from Cleopatra Beach to Alanya center (1.5 km), the coastal promenade is flat and pleasant — older travelers can walk in 25 min and skip the taxi.
scams.avoidance: Insist on meter for taxis; confirm ₺140–₺200 range to Cleopatra Beach before boarding Use BiTaksi app for app-regulated fares Book boat tours via hotel concierge or vetted operator at ₺600–₺900/person Decline beach-tout 'special tours' under €15 — the math forces shortcuts and tip demands Walk the 1.5 km coastal promenade back to Alanya center (25 min) instead of taxi
scams.location: Cleopatra Beach taxi rank, Damlataş Caddesi pickup zones, Alanya Marina boat-tour booking offices, Portacall (Liman) ferry transfers

scams.name: Restaurant Pricing Inflation & 'Tourist Menu' Doubling
scams.description: Alanya's restaurant strip operates on the standard Turkish tourist-belt model: English-language laminated menus with photos and no prices, touts on the sidewalk recruiting passing tourists, drinks priced 4–5x local rates, and bills that arrive 30–60% above the menu prices that were shown. One traveler wrote: 'Prices have actually tripled or even quadrupled over the last 2 years. Compared to when I first came to Turkey' the basic dining math has shifted. Community trip reports from 2025 confirm the escalation across Turkish tourist zones. The specific Alanya patterns: (1) 'menü' boards in English with photos but no prices; (2) bread, olives, meze 'complimentary' that cost ₺50–₺100 per item on the bill; (3) 'fish of the day' priced 'per kilo' with weight inflated; (4) cover charges (kuver) of ₺50–₺80 per person not disclosed at seating; (5) 'tourist set menu' at ₺800–₺1,200 for what local restaurants charge ₺300–₺450. One traveler gave the single-line rule: 'If a restaurant has a dude out front who comes up even before you look at the menu, keep walking.' For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) avoid Bar Street and Cleopatra Beach strip restaurants with English-only photo menus; (2) walk one block back from the seafront to find restaurants where Turkish residents eat — community-recommended Alanya names: Köşem Restaurant (Atatürk Caddesi, Turkish home cooking), Sofra (Old Town, regional specialties), Mahmutlar Manti House (Mahmutlar, posted prices); (3) for fish, ask to see the fish before ordering AND have it weighed in your presence, get the per-kg price IN WRITING; (4) refuse complimentary bread/olives unless prices are confirmed; (5) check the bill line-by-line and dispute any item not ordered; (6) bargaining is expected and not rude — 30–40% off the first quote is reasonable in tourist-tier shops.
scams.avoidance: Walk one block off Bar Street/Cleopatra strip to find restaurants for Turkish residents Community-recommended: Köşem Restaurant (Atatürk Caddesi), Sofra (Old Town), Mahmutlar Manti House For fish, see it weighed in your presence and get per-kg price in writing Refuse complimentary bread/olives unless prices are confirmed Check bill line-by-line; dispute any item not ordered
scams.location: Restaurants on Bar Street (Damlataş Caddesi), Cleopatra Beach restaurant strip, Alanya Old Town tourist alleys, Mahmutlar all-inclusive resort area exterior

scams.name: Antalya (AYT) & Gazipaşa (GZP) Airport Transfer Overcharge
scams.description: Alanya is served by two airports: Antalya (AYT) 130 km west and Gazipaşa-Alanya (GZP) 40 km east. Most package-holiday travelers arrive via AYT — the legitimate licensed taxi fare from AYT to Alanya is approximately ₺2,000–₺2,500 (€50–€63) on the meter for the 130 km journey. From GZP, the fare to central Alanya is ₺600–₺900 (€15–€22). Unofficial operators at AYT quote 'fixed prices' of €100–€150 for the same trip; from GZP €40–€60. One traveler wrote: 'Biggest scam are taxis, they'll charge you 2x 3x as soon as they notice you are a foreigner.' Community reports recommend BiTaksi for app-regulated fares. Most package-tour operators (TUI, Jet2, easyJet Holidays, Tez Tour, Anex Tour) include free coach transfer from AYT — the cheapest and most overcharge-proof option for older travelers with luggage. For independent travelers, the practical playbook: (1) confirm whether your tour operator includes free coach transfer BEFORE arrival and wait at the designated meeting point; (2) for AYT, the Havaş airport bus serves Alanya otogar at ₺250 per person (~€6.50, 2.5 hr) — the budget-friendly independent option; (3) if taking a metered taxi from AYT, confirm the ₺2,000–₺2,500 range upfront and insist on Tarife 1 (day rate); (4) for GZP, the airport is small and the metered fare to Alanya is straightforward — refuse 'fixed price' quotes over €30; (5) book Welcome Pickups in advance for AYT-to-Alanya transfer (€60–€80 per car for up to 4 people) — vetted operators with fixed prices; (6) Uber does NOT operate in Alanya; only BiTaksi and licensed taxis are legitimate.
scams.avoidance: Confirm package-tour transfer is included with TUI/Jet2/Tez Tour/Anex Tour before arrival From AYT, take Havaş bus to Alanya otogar (₺250, 2.5 hr) for budget independent travel If using metered taxi from AYT, confirm ₺2,000–₺2,500 range and insist on Tarife 1 Book Welcome Pickups for AYT-to-Alanya (€60–€80 per car for 4) Pre-book late-night Bar Street returns through hotel reception
scams.location: Antalya Airport (AYT) taxi rank, Gazipaşa-Alanya Airport (GZP) taxi rank, hotel-concierge transfers, late-night returns from Bar Street nightlife

scams.name: All-Inclusive Resort Excursion Reseller & Hotel Tout Markups
scams.description: Alanya is one of Europe's largest German, Russian, and Scandinavian package-tour markets, with a dense ecosystem of all-inclusive resorts on the Mahmutlar–Avsallar–Konaklı strip. The standard scam: hotel concierges and beach-promenade tour offices sell €60–€120 'all-inclusive day excursions' to nearby attractions (Manavgat Waterfall, Side Ancient City, Aspendos Theatre, Alanya Castle) that bundle into the price 2–3 'demonstration' or 'cooperative' shopping stops — onyx jewelry, Turkish delight, leather, carpets — each paying the operator a 30–40% commission. Community reports. Reports from 2025 confirm that legitimate vetted operators do exist but require active vetting, and the broader package-belt context remains the same. For older travelers on package holidays, the practical playbook: (1) avoid hotel-concierge excursion sales — these are commission-driven referrals; (2) for legitimate excursions, book directly via GetYourGuide or Viator with 'no shopping stops' filter active and verify TÜRSAB Turkish Ministry of Culture licensing; (3) Manavgat Waterfall + Side day-trip should cost €30–€50 per person via vetted small-group operators; (4) for Aspendos Theatre, book a private driver (€80–€120 round-trip from Alanya for up to 4 people) instead of bus tours that include shopping; (5) if a tour stops at a 'demonstration' or 'cooperative,' stay on the bus and refuse to enter; (6) for Alanya Castle and Cleopatra Beach, no excursion is needed — these are walkable from central Alanya hotels.
scams.avoidance: Avoid hotel-concierge excursion sales (commission-driven referrals) Book directly via GetYourGuide or Viator with 'no shopping stops' filter and TÜRSAB licensing verified Manavgat + Side day-trip should be €30–€50 per person at vetted operators For Aspendos, hire a private driver (€80–€120 round-trip for up to 4) instead of bus tours If tour stops at 'demonstration' or 'cooperative,' stay on the bus and refuse to enter
scams.location: All-inclusive hotel concierge desks (Mahmutlar, Avsallar, Konaklı), beach-promenade tour booking offices, hotel-arranged 'special excursion' packages

scams.name: Damlataş Cave & Castle 'Skip-the-Line' Tout Scams
scams.description: Alanya Castle and Damlataş Cave are the city's headline cultural attractions. Damlataş Cave entry is ₺120 (~€3); Alanya Castle entry is ₺240 (~€6); Red Tower is ₺120 (~€3). The cable car to the castle is ₺200 round-trip (~€5). All four are inexpensive walk-up attractions with rare queues. The scam: touts at the entrance approach foreigners offering 'skip-the-line' tickets at €15–€25 per person, claiming the official queue is 'closed today' or that a 'special bundle pass' is required. One traveler offered the broader Antalya-region rule: 'If a shop doesn't have price tags, it's likely a tourist scam. If it's located in a touristy area, it's tourist-tier extraction.' Community reports confirm the broader Alanya tout ecosystem operating around all the major attractions, with 2025 reports reinforcing the same regional context. For older travelers, the practical playbook: (1) walk past all touts to the official ticket booth at each attraction; (2) Damlataş Cave: ₺120 (~€3), useful for 15-min visit, indoor and accessible; (3) Alanya Castle: ₺240 (~€6) — the cable car (₺200) is recommended for older travelers given the steep walk; (4) Red Tower: ₺120 (~€3); (5) for a Castle + Cable Car + Damlataş Cave combo experience, the total is under €15 per person paid at official booths; (6) decline 'skip-the-line' offers — none of these attractions has queues except briefly during cruise mornings; (7) buy water, snacks, and evil-eye souvenirs at Migros or supermarket stalls before the climb — the castle vendors charge 3x.
scams.avoidance: Walk past all touts to the official ticket booth at each attraction Damlataş Cave ₺120, Alanya Castle ₺240, Red Tower ₺120, Cable Car ₺200 round-trip — all official prices under €6 Combined experience under €15 per person paid at official booths Decline 'skip-the-line' offers — these attractions rarely have queues Buy water, snacks, evil-eye souvenirs at Migros before the climb
scams.location: Damlataş Cave entrance area, Alanya Castle (Alanya Kalesi) approach paths, cable-car queue, Red Tower (Kızıl Kule) ticket area
